within_list_cues.VA01: Trap value 3 is listed twice (unscaled sum of x + 2y = 8 and b). Harmless for SPR, but list it once. No other cue.
within_list_cues.VA05: Moot (drop). The choices also allow plugging (5, 5) and (0, 8) to eliminate A, B and D without the inequality argument.
within_list_cues.VA08: Plugging any one value of m (e.g. 0) gives the key; that is the math itself here, acceptable. A/D are a sign pair, so the key is one of a pair; acceptable and common.
within_list_cues.VA09: Moot (drop). Also, the 66.67 trap is not an integer count and is eliminated by common sense in SPR.
within_list_cues.VA10: Trap '-18, multiplies instead of dividing' has no reproducible derivation (multiplying by -4 gives -72; by -1/4 is the key). Replace or remove.
within_list_cues.VA12: Moot (drop). Also a given value that is irrelevant: every line with b = 3m (m != 0) has x-intercept -3, so the point (1, 8) never affects the answer; the generator itself notes this.
within_list_cues.VA13: Choices A (y + 3 = 2(x - 1)) and C (y - 3 = 2(x - 1)) differ only by one sign, so a test-taker narrows to that pair. Plugging (3, 1) into each choice finds the key; that is the intended check. Mild; acceptable.
within_list_cues.VC04: Key D is the only statement about the sample and the only certain one, so a test-taker who knows 'must be true' excludes anything about the population can pick it without understanding margin of error. Make one distractor a false sample-level statement, e.g. 'Between 20 and 40 of the 500 adults in the sample gave inaccurate answers' (margin of error read as a count of errors), replacing C or B.
within_list_cues.VC06: Key B is the only hedged causal claim ('likely causes'); A and D state causation flatly. Hedge one distractor too (e.g. A: 'Volunteering likely causes ... for the city's adults, because ...').
within_list_cues.VC07: Key A is the longest choice (177 characters vs 147-156). Trim it, e.g. 'The students chose whether to attend, so other differences between the groups could explain the result.'
within_list_cues.VC08: Trap 80 ('the remaining 80 miles must take 1 hour') has no natural derivation; remove it. The 65 (distance-weighted average) and 70 (plain average) traps are good.
within_list_cues.VC13: The key 12 equals the mean of the data (and the added value), so a student who reports the mean, or assumes median = mean, gets credit without finding the median. Change the data so the added value is not the middle number: e.g. 2, 3, 4, 5, 20, 26 (mean 10, original median 4.5); add 10 -> 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20, 26, median 5. Traps: 10 (the mean/added value), 4.5 (original median), 70 (new sum).
within_list_cues.none (others): VA02, VA03, VA06, VA07, VA11, VA15, VC01, VC02, VC05, VC09, VC10, VC11, VC12, VC14, VC15: no length, odd-one-out, common-sense or calculator-shortcut cue found; every needed value is given in the data items (VC14 intercept point given; VC15 all four cells given).
